Loss-of-function mutations in LARGE1 impair the glycosylation of dystroglycan, a key component of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex. This impaired glycosylation leads to instability of the complex and downstream effects on muscle integrity and potentially neuronal development, manifesting as congenital muscular dystrophy and neurological phenotypes. Loss-of-function mutations in LARGE1 impair the glycosylation of dystroglycan, a key component of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex. This impaired glycosylation leads to instability of the complex and downstream effects on muscle integrity and potentially neuronal development, manifesting as congenital muscular dystrophy and neurological phenotypes.
